summary.text: James Gallagher is an attorney and farmer from Sutter County who served on the Sutter County Board of Supervisors and then in the California State Assembly from 2014 to 2026, including as Assembly Minority Leader from 2022 to 2025. He won the June 2, 2026 special election outright to fill the House seat left vacant by the death of Rep. Doug LaMalfa and is also running for a full term. His stated campaign messages are lower taxes, lower fees and fewer regulations, tougher laws against crime, and protecting farms and businesses from regulation.

paragraphs.text: Gallagher was born in Yuba City in 1981 and attended local schools, according to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response. He describes himself as a descendant of Irish immigrants who settled in northern California in the early 1800s.
He earned a high school diploma from East Nicolaus High School, a B.A. from UC Berkeley, and a law degree from UC Davis, and he also completed an Assembly Fellowship in Sacramento.
He worked as an attorney in a practice centered on business and agriculture and is a partner in his family's rice farm.
Gallagher served on the Sutter County Board of Supervisors for six years before joining the Assembly.

He represented California's Third Assembly District from 2014 to 2026; Roll Call describes the district as an inland district centered on Chico. His committee service included the Judiciary Committee, on which he was Vice Chair.
He was Assembly Minority Leader from 2022 to 2025, leading Republican legislators in opposing the 2025 redistricting effort, and Roll Call reports he stepped down as caucus leader in September 2025.

Roll Call reports that the Public Policy Institute of California credited Gallagher with paying particular attention to small businesses and farms and with dozens of enacted bills, including a measure to facilitate housing relief for victims of the 2018 Camp Fire.

He won the June 2, 2026 special primary for California's 1st District with more than 60 percent of the vote, avoiding an August runoff, and was sworn in on June 10, 2026 to complete the term of the late Rep. Doug LaMalfa. He also advanced from the regular June 2 primary for the full term.

According to his Ballotpedia survey response, Gallagher is married and lives in Sutter County with his family, and he is passionate about wildfire mitigation, water storage, supporting farms and small businesses, and neighborhood safety.

sources.title: James Gallagher sworn in to finish LaMalfa's term in the House
